    33	/-- A tempered measure: `∫ (1 + ‖x‖)^(-k) dν < ∞` for some natural `k`. -/

    44	def IsPosDefDistr {d : ℕ} (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    45	  ∀ φ : SchwartzMap (Rd d) ℂ,
    46	    (∫ x, (∫ y, φ (x + y) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (φ y)) ∂Γ).im = 0 ∧

    61	/-! ### (1) The Hilbert-space inequality (TeX l. 365-368) -/
    62	
    63	/-- `‖Σ c_j v_j‖² ≤ (Σ |c_j|) Σ |c_j| ‖v_j‖²` for a finite family in a complex
    64	seminormed space (in particular in any complex inner product space). -/
    65	theorem norm_sq_sum_le {ι E : Type*} [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E]
    66	    (s : Finset ι) (c : ι → ℂ) (v : ι → E) :
    67	    ‖∑ j ∈ s, c j • v j‖ ^ 2 ≤
    68	      (∑ j ∈ s, ‖c j‖) * ∑ j ∈ s, ‖c j‖ * ‖v j‖ ^ 2 := by
    69	  have htri : ‖∑ j ∈ s, c j • v j‖ ≤ ∑ j ∈ s, ‖c j‖ * ‖v j‖ := by
    70	    refine (norm_sum_le _ _).trans (le_of_eq ?_)
    71	    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ => norm_smul _ _
    72	  have hcs : (∑ j ∈ s, ‖c j‖ * ‖v j‖) ^ 2 ≤
    73	      (∑ j ∈ s, ‖c j‖) * ∑ j ∈ s, ‖c j‖ * ‖v j‖ ^ 2 := by
    74	    have key := Finset.sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq s (fun j => Real.sqrt ‖c j‖)
    75	      (fun j => Real.sqrt ‖c j‖ * ‖v j‖)
    76	    have e1 : ∀ j, Real.sqrt ‖c j‖ * (Real.sqrt ‖c j‖ * ‖v j‖) = ‖c j‖ * ‖v j‖ :=
    77	      fun j => by rw [← mul_assoc, Real.mul_self_sqrt (norm_nonneg _)]
    78	    have e2 : ∀ j, Real.sqrt ‖c j‖ ^ 2 = ‖c j‖ :=
    79	      fun j => Real.sq_sqrt (norm_nonneg _)
    80	    have e3 : ∀ j, (Real.sqrt ‖c j‖ * ‖v j‖) ^ 2 = ‖c j‖ * ‖v j‖ ^ 2 :=
    81	      fun j => by rw [mul_pow, e2]
    82	    simp only [e1, e2, e3] at key
    83	    exact key
    84	  have h0 : 0 ≤ ‖∑ j ∈ s, c j • v j‖ := norm_nonneg _
    85	  calc ‖∑ j ∈ s, c j • v j‖ ^ 2 ≤ (∑ j ∈ s, ‖c j‖ * ‖v j‖) ^ 2 :=
    86	        pow_le_pow_left₀ h0 htri 2
    87	    _ ≤ _ := hcs
    88	
    89	/-- The same inequality, stated in a complex inner product space (the
    90	manuscript's "In a Hilbert space"). -/
    91	theorem norm_sq_sum_le_inner {ι E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℂ E]
    92	    (s : Finset ι) (c : ι → ℂ) (v : ι → E) :
    93	    ‖∑ j ∈ s, c j • v j‖ ^ 2 ≤
    94	      (∑ j ∈ s, ‖c j‖) * ∑ j ∈ s, ‖c j‖ * ‖v j‖ ^ 2 :=
    95	  norm_sq_sum_le s c v

    97	/-! ### Definitions -/
    98	
    99	/-- Japanese bracket `⟨x⟩ = √(1+x²)` (TeX l. 296). -/
   100	def bracket (x : ℝ) : ℝ := Real.sqrt (1 + x ^ 2)
   101	
   102	theorem bracket_neg (x : ℝ) : bracket (-x) = bracket x := by
   103	  simp [bracket]
   104	
   105	/-- `𝒬_h(r,ρ) = ⟨h(r-ρ)⟩^{a-1} + ⟨h(r+ρ)⟩^{a-1}` (TeX l. 355-358). -/
   106	def frequencyPair (a h r ρ : ℝ) : ℝ :=
   107	  bracket (h * (r - ρ)) ^ (a - 1) + bracket (h * (r + ρ)) ^ (a - 1)
   108	
   109	/-- The two trigonometric factor shapes `cos` and `sin`. -/
   110	inductive Trig
   111	  | cos
   112	  | sin
   113	  deriving DecidableEq
   114	
   115	/-- `Trig.eval k x` is `cos x` or `sin x`, viewed in `ℂ`. -/
   116	def Trig.eval : Trig → ℝ → ℂ
   117	  | .cos, x => (Real.cos x : ℂ)
   118	  | .sin, x => (Real.sin x : ℂ)
   119	
   120	/-- The modulated amplitude `t ↦ 1_I(t) A(t) e^{iωt}`. -/
   121	def modeFn (I : Set ℝ) (A : ℝ → ℂ) (ω : ℝ) : ℝ → ℂ :=
   122	  I.indicator fun t => A t * Complex.exp (((ω * t : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I)
   123	
   124	/-- The product `t ↦ 1_I(t) A(t) P_r(t) Q_ρ(t)`. -/
   125	def prodFn (I : Set ℝ) (A : ℝ → ℂ) (P Q : Trig) (r ρ : ℝ) : ℝ → ℂ :=
   126	  I.indicator fun t => A t * P.eval (r * t) * Q.eval (ρ * t)
   127	
   128	/-- The sign `σ ∈ {1, -1}`, indexed by `Bool`. -/
   129	def sgn : Bool → ℝ
   130	  | true => 1
   131	  | false => -1
   132	
   133	/-- Coefficients of a single factor: `cos x = ½e^{ix} + ½e^{-ix}`,
   134	`sin x = (-i/2)e^{ix} + (i/2)e^{-ix}`. -/
   135	def coef1 : Trig → Bool → ℂ
   136	  | .cos, _ => 1 / 2
   137	  | .sin, true => -Complex.I / 2
   138	  | .sin, false => Complex.I / 2
   139	
   140	/-- Coefficient of the mode `e^{i(σr+τρ)t}` in `P_r Q_ρ`. -/
   141	def coef (P Q : Trig) (j : Bool × Bool) : ℂ := coef1 P j.1 * coef1 Q j.2
   142	
   143	/-- Frequency `σr + τρ` of the mode indexed by `j = (σ, τ)`. -/
   144	def freq (r ρ : ℝ) (j : Bool × Bool) : ℝ := sgn j.1 * r + sgn j.2 * ρ
   145	
   146	/-! ### (2) The four-mode expansions (TeX l. 363-365) -/
   147	
   148	theorem norm_coef1 (k : Trig) (σ : Bool) : ‖coef1 k σ‖ = 1 / 2 := by
   149	  cases k <;> cases σ <;> simp [coef1]
   150	
   151	/-- Every coefficient has absolute value `1/4`. -/
   152	theorem norm_coef (P Q : Trig) (j : Bool × Bool) : ‖coef P Q j‖ = 1 / 4 := by
   153	  rw [coef, norm_mul, norm_coef1, norm_coef1]; norm_num
   154	
   155	/-- The coefficient sum `Σ|c_j|` is one (TeX l. 370). -/
   156	theorem sum_norm_coef (P Q : Trig) : ∑ j : Bool × Bool, ‖coef P Q j‖ = 1 := by
   157	  simp only [norm_coef, Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_prod,
   158	    Fintype.card_bool, nsmul_eq_mul]
   159	  norm_num
   160	
   161	theorem exp_sgn (σ : Bool) (x : ℝ) :
   162	    Complex.exp (((sgn σ * x : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I) =
   163	      if σ then Complex.exp ((x : ℂ) * Complex.I)
   164	      else Complex.exp (-((x : ℂ) * Complex.I)) := by
   165	  cases σ <;> simp [sgn]
   166	
   167	/-- One-factor expansion. -/
   168	theorem Trig.eval_expand (k : Trig) (x : ℝ) :
   169	    k.eval x = ∑ σ : Bool, coef1 k σ * Complex.exp (((sgn σ * x : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I) := by
   170	  simp only [Fintype.sum_bool, exp_sgn, ite_true, Bool.false_eq_true, ite_false]
   171	  cases k
   172	  · simp only [Trig.eval, coef1, Complex.ofReal_cos, Complex.cos, neg_mul]
   173	    ring
   174	  · simp only [Trig.eval, coef1, Complex.ofReal_sin, Complex.sin, neg_mul]
   175	    field_simp
   176	    ring
   177	
   178	/-- The generic four-mode expansion: `P_r(t) Q_ρ(t) = Σ_{σ,τ} c_{στ} e^{i(σr+τρ)t}`
   179	with `|c_{στ}| = 1/4` (`norm_coef`). -/
   180	theorem four_mode (P Q : Trig) (r ρ t : ℝ) :
   181	    P.eval (r * t) * Q.eval (ρ * t) =
   182	      ∑ j : Bool × Bool, coef P Q j * Complex.exp (((freq r ρ j * t : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I) := by
   183	  rw [P.eval_expand, Q.eval_expand, Finset.sum_mul_sum, ← Finset.univ_product_univ,
   184	    Finset.sum_product]
   185	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun σ _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun τ _ => ?_
   186	  simp only [coef, freq]
   187	  have : (((sgn σ * r + sgn τ * ρ) * t : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I =
   188	      ((sgn σ * (r * t) : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I + ((sgn τ * (ρ * t) : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I := by
   189	    push_cast; ring
   190	  rw [this, Complex.exp_add]
     1	\section{Frequency estimates and both wave variance directions}
     2	\label{S:wave-variance}
     3	
     4	We now apply the covariance and temporal estimates of
     5	Section~\ref{S:masked-covariance} to the full wave phase. We retain
     6	Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, write $a = \alpha_0$, and choose and fix
     7	\begin{equation}\label{E:variance-gamma-range}
     8	  0 < \gamma < \min\left(\frac12,\frac{2-\alpha}{2}\right).
     9	\end{equation}
    10	The interval is nonempty because $\alpha+a < 2$. We use $\langle\xi\rangle =
    11	\sqrt{1+|\xi|^2}$ and set
    12	\begin{equation}\label{E:variance-scale-profile}
    13	  B_\alpha(h) =
    14	  \begin{cases}
    15	    1, & \alpha < 1,\\
    16	    1+\log(1/h), & \alpha = 1,\\
    17	    h^{1-\alpha}, & \alpha > 1,
    18	  \end{cases}
    19	  \qquad 0 < h \le 1.
    20	\end{equation}
    21	
    22	\subsection{A scalar row estimate for a measure}
    23	
    24	Let $\nu$ be a positive Radon measure satisfying
    25	\begin{equation}\label{E:frequency-translated-growth}
    26	  \nu(B(y,r)) \le C r^\alpha,
    27	  \qquad y \in \R^d,\quad r > 0,
    28	\end{equation}
    29	where $C \ge 0$. If the estimate is initially known for open balls, apply it at
    30	radius $r+\epsilon$ and let $\epsilon \downarrow 0$ to obtain the closed-ball
    31	estimate. Neither evenness nor a density is assumed here.
    32	Using~\eqref{E:masked-frequency-pair}, define
    33	\begin{align}
    34	  \Phi_h(\xi,\eta)
    35	  &:= \frac{\mathcal{Q}_h(|\xi|,|\eta|)}
    36	  {\langle\xi\rangle\langle\eta\rangle},
    37	  \label{E:frequency-row-kernel}\\
    38	  J_h(\xi)
    39	  &:= \langle\xi\rangle^{2\gamma}
    40	  \int_{\R^d}\Phi_h(\xi,\xi-\lambda)\nu(\ud\lambda).
    41	  \label{E:frequency-row-integral}
    42	\end{align}
    43	These are initially nonnegative extended integrals. In particular, the notation
    44	denotes a pushforward of $\nu$, not integration against an assumed spectral
    45	density.
    46	
    47	\begin{proposition}[Uniform scalar row]\label{P:frequency-row}
    48	  There is a finite $K = K(\alpha,a,\gamma)$, independent of $d,\nu,C,h$ and
    49	  $\xi$, such that
    50	  \begin{equation}\label{E:frequency-row-bound}
    51	    \sup_{\xi\in\R^d}J_h(\xi) \le K C B_\alpha(h),
    52	    \qquad 0 < h \le 1.
    53	  \end{equation}
    54	\end{proposition}
    55	
    56	\begin{proof}
    57	  If $C = 0$, a countable covering by finite balls gives $\nu = 0$, and the
    58	  result is immediate. Suppose $C > 0$. For each $\xi$, let $\nu_\xi$ be the
    59	  pushforward under $\lambda \mapsto \eta = \xi-\lambda$. Then $\nu_\xi(B(0,R))
    60	  \le CR^\alpha$. For $q \ge 1$, put
    61	  \[
    62	    A_\xi(q) = \int_{|\eta|\le5q}\langle\eta\rangle^{-1}
    63	    \nu_\xi(\ud\eta).
    64	  \]
    65	  Choose $N = \lceil\log_2(5q)\rceil$, so $5q \le 2^N < 10q$. Splitting into the
    66	  unit ball and the annuli $2^j < |\eta| \le 2^{j+1}$ gives
    67	  \[
    68	    A_\xi(q) \le C\left(1+2^\alpha
    69	    \sum_{j=0}^{N-1}2^{j(\alpha-1)}\right).
    70	  \]
    71	  The geometric sum is bounded when $\alpha < 1$, is $N$ when $\alpha = 1$, and
    72	  is at most $2^{N(\alpha-1)}/(2^{\alpha-1}-1)$ when $\alpha > 1$. Hence,
    73	  \begin{equation}\label{E:frequency-inverse-bessel}
    74	    A_\xi(q) \le K_\alpha C
    75	    \begin{cases}
    76	      1, & \alpha < 1,\\
    77	      1+\log q, & \alpha = 1,\\
    78	      q^{\alpha-1}, & \alpha > 1,
    79	    \end{cases}
    80	  \end{equation}
    81	  with a constant depending only on $\alpha$.
    82	
    83	  Set $q = \max(1,|\xi|)$ and $\epsilon = 1-2\gamma > 0$. On $|\lambda| \le 4q$
    84	  we have $|\eta| \le 5q$. Both bracket powers in $\mathcal{Q}_h$ are at most
    85	  one, since $a-1 < 0$. The contribution of this region to $J_h(\xi)$ is at most
    86	  \[
    87	    2\langle\xi\rangle^{-\epsilon}A_\xi(q)
    88	    \le 2q^{-\epsilon}A_\xi(q).
    89	  \]
    90	  If $\alpha < 1$, this is uniformly bounded
    91	  by~\eqref{E:frequency-inverse-bessel}. If $\alpha = 1$, the bound follows from
    92	  \[
    93	    e^{-\epsilon u}(1+u) \le 1+\frac1{e\epsilon},
    94	    \qquad u = \log q \ge 0,
    95	  \]
    96	  since $u e^{-\epsilon u}$ has maximum $1/(e\epsilon)$. If $\alpha > 1$, the
    97	  remaining power is $q^{\alpha+2\gamma-2}$, whose exponent is negative
    98	  by~\eqref{E:variance-gamma-range}. Thus, the near contribution is at most a
    99	  constant times $C$ in all three cases.
   100	
   101	  On the far region write $r = |\lambda| > 4q$. Then
   102	  \[
   103	    |\eta| \ge \frac{3r}4,\qquad
   104	    \big||\eta|-|\xi|\big| \ge \frac r2,\qquad
   105	    |\eta|+|\xi| \ge \frac r2.
   106	  \]
   107	  Each oscillatory bracket is at least $\langle hr\rangle/2$, whereas
   108	  $\langle\eta\rangle^{-1} \le 4/(3r)$ and $\langle\xi\rangle^{-\epsilon} \le
   109	  1$. Consequently, the far contribution is at most
   110	  \[
   111	    \frac43\,2^{2-a}\int_{|\lambda|>4q}
   112	    |\lambda|^{-1}\langle h|\lambda|\rangle^{a-1}\nu(\ud\lambda).
   113	  \]
   114	  Enlarge the domain to $|\lambda| > 1$ and split it into dyadic annuli.
   115	  Applying~\eqref{E:frequency-translated-growth} to their masses bounds this
   116	  expression by a constant depending only on $\alpha,a$ times $C S(h)$, where
   117	  \[
   118	    S(h) = \sum_{j=0}^\infty
   119	    2^{j(\alpha-1)}\langle h2^j\rangle^{a-1}.
   120	  \]
   121	  Choose $L = \lfloor\log_2(1/h)\rfloor \ge 0$. For $j \le L$ the bracket power
   122	  is at most one. For $j \ge L+1$ it is at most $(h2^j)^{a-1}$. Since
   123	  $\alpha+a-2 < 0$, the tail is
   124	  \[
   125	    \frac{h^{a-1}2^{(L+1)(\alpha+a-2)}}{1-2^{\alpha+a-2}}
   126	    \le \frac{h^{1-\alpha}}{1-2^{\alpha+a-2}}.
   127	  \]
   128	  The inequality uses $2^{L+1} > 1/h$ and the negative exponent. The finite sum
   129	  is bounded by $1/(1-2^{\alpha-1})$ for $\alpha < 1$, by $1+\log_2(1/h)$ for
   130	  $\alpha = 1$, and by
   131	  \[
   132	    \frac{2^{\alpha-1}h^{1-\alpha}}{2^{\alpha-1}-1}
   133	  \]
   134	  for $\alpha > 1$. Since $h^{1-\alpha} \le 1$ in the first case, we obtain
   135	  $S(h) \le K_{\alpha,a}B_\alpha(h)$. Combining the near and far bounds, and
   136	  using $B_\alpha(h) \ge 1$, proves the assertion and finiteness of the original
   137	  integral. All constants arose from numerical shell estimates and are
   138	  independent of $d$. This proves Proposition~\ref{P:frequency-row}.
   139	\end{proof}
   140	
   141	\begin{corollary}[A time exponent above one half]\label{C:frequency-time}
   142	  For every
   143	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-beta-range}
   144	    \frac12 < \beta < \min\left(1-\frac a2,
   145	    \frac{3-a-\alpha}{2}\right),
   146	  \end{equation}
   147	  there is a finite $K_\beta = K_\beta(\alpha,a,\gamma,\beta)$ such that
   148	  \begin{equation}\label{E:frequency-time-bound}

   164	  This proves Corollary~\ref{C:frequency-time}.

1	# Statement ledger
     2	
     3	This ledger maps labels of the manuscript on the second moment of the
     4	Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model with Gaussian noise fractional in time
     5	to the Lean declarations in this package. Labels refer to the manuscript
     6	revision 3920258 and are written exactly as in its LaTeX source (for
     7	example `P:clock-copy-obstruction`). The ledger was written and reviewed
     8	at the earlier revisions cf979d6, 669ccc9 and ba01d98. The later revisions
     9	changed only prose, titles, the literature review, layout and figures:
    10	every cited label exists in all four, and the mathematical expressions of
    11	each cited statement and its proof are the same up to whitespace and braces
    12	(script checks recorded in `provenance/manuscript-anchor.json`).
    13	
    14	## Scope
    15	
    16	- The "What it states" column is a faithful paraphrase, sometimes
    17	  shortened. The exact statement is the Lean type in
    18	  `StratonovichHAMAudit/<Module>.lean`; `Audit/<module>/` prints the
    19	  elaborated types.
    20	- The rows cover every public theorem (611) and 113 definitions whose
    21	  values are stated as facts or that name a manuscript object. The other
    22	  49 public definitions (for example
    23	  `kappa`, `delta`, `gauge`, `counts`) only name quantities used in those
    24	  statements and have no rows of their own; read their bodies in the Lean
    25	  source or in `Audit/`.
    26	- The `StratonovichHAMAudit` modules check finite, algebraic and scalar
    27	  steps only: exact identities, polynomial and rational certificates,
    28	  real-power bookkeeping, parameter ranges, and a few finite-dimensional
    29	  inner-product and finite-word facts.
    30	- The twenty-six `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment` modules (sections marked
    31	  "whole result" below; four of them are the wave-kernel and
    32	  time-fractional foundation of `ClockCopy`, and `GaussianTest` is the
    33	  Gaussian-test foundation of `MaskedSpectralGrowth`) model `H:homog` and
    34	  formalize the conclusions of twenty-three
    35	  labelled results in full. Twenty need no supplied input:
    36	  `L:gaussian-scalar-powers` is stated with the manuscript's own
    37	  hypotheses. `L:gram-scalar-algebra` and `L:tube-rayleigh-tail` are
    38	  proved under weaker hypotheses (no completeness or `C_ij >= 0`; no

    41	  Rayleigh lemma's "In particular" application to another proposition is

    43	  numerical part of `H:homog` (a generalization) and also restated under
    44	  the full hypothesis `H:homog`, which `HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance`
    45	  models clause by clause (covariance measure, spectral measure, evenness,

    49	  `temporal_equilibrium_paper`). The finite slice of `S:compact-gaussian`,

  1063	## FrequencyRow (whole result)
  1064	
  1065	Formalizes Proposition `P:frequency-row` (lines 47-139) and Corollary
  1066	`C:frequency-time` (lines 141-165) of `notes/integrated_wave_variance.tex` at
  1067	`3920258` (the file is byte-identical at `ba01d98`, so the line numbers hold
  1068	for both revisions). It also formalizes the definitions `E:variance-scale-profile`
  1069	(lines 12-20), `E:frequency-row-kernel` (lines 33-37) and
  1070	`E:frequency-row-integral` (lines 38-42), and the closed-ball remark after
  1071	`E:frequency-translated-growth` (lines 29-31). `bracket` and `frequencyPair`
  1072	(`Q_h` of `E:masked-frequency-pair`) are reused from `MaskedTrigProducts`.
  1073	`J_h(xi)` is a lower Lebesgue integral in `[0, inf]`, the "nonnegative
  1074	extended integral" of line 43, so no Bochner junk value enters its
  1075	definition. Nothing is supplied as a hypothesis.
  1076	
  1077	The quantifier order is exactly `exists K, forall d nu C h xi`. `frequency_row`
  1078	proves `exists K >= 0, forall d (nu a measure on R^d) C, C >= 0 -> growth -> forall h,
  1079	0 < h -> h <= 1 ->` `sup_xi J_h(xi) <= K C B_alpha(h)`. It also proves, for each
  1080	`xi`, `nu`-integrability of `lambda -> Phi_h(xi, xi-lambda)` and the real-integral
  1081	bound `<xi>^(2 gamma) int Phi_h(xi,xi-lambda) nu(dlambda) <= K C B_alpha(h)`
  1082	(the finiteness at lines 136-137). Its hypotheses are `a < 1`,
  1083	`alpha + a < 2`, `2 gamma <= 1` and `alpha + 2 gamma < 2`. The section's
  1084	range `0 < gamma < min(1/2, (2-alpha)/2)` (`E:variance-gamma-range`, lines 7-9)
  1085	implies the last two. `frequency_time` has the same form,
  1086	`exists K_beta >= 0, forall d nu C h`, with the extra hypotheses
  1087	`2 beta < 2 - a` and `2 beta < 3 - a - alpha`. The `_paper` wrappers take the
  1088	section's hypotheses: `H:homog` with `a = alpha0` as
  1089	`HomogCovariance d alpha a Gamma mu` (lines 5-6), the range of `gamma`, a
  1090	locally finite (Radon) `nu`, `C >= 0` and the growth bound. The corollary also
  1091	takes `1/2 < beta < min(1 - a/2, (3-a-alpha)/2)` (`E:variance-beta-range`,
  1092	lines 143-145). In the wrappers the constant is chosen before
  1093	`d, Gamma, mu, nu, C, h` (and `xi`).
  1094	
  1095	Implicit hypotheses made explicit: `B(y,r)` in
  1096	`E:frequency-translated-growth` is read as the open ball, the weaker
  1097	hypothesis, and `closedBall_le` derives the closed-ball bound. `nu` is a
  1098	measure on the Borel sigma-algebra. Measurability of the kernel is proved,
  1099	not assumed. Integrability is part of the conclusion.
  1100	
  1101	Hypotheses carried but unused (wrappers): `gamma > 0`, `beta > 1/2`, local
  1102	finiteness of `nu`, and all of `H:homog` except `alpha0 < 1` and
  1103	`alpha0 + alpha < 2`. The general theorems hold for every `d`, including
  1104	`d = 0`, and every real `alpha` meeting their numerical hypotheses.
  1105	
  1106	Proof route. The integrand is bounded pointwise by two dyadic shell
  1107	majorants of closed balls of radius `2^j`: one around `xi` on the near region
  1108	`|lambda| <= 4|xi|`, one around `0` on the far region. The TeX splits at
  1109	`4q`, `q = max(1,|xi|)`. On the near region `<xi> >= 2^n/5` gives the single
  1110	ratio `2^(alpha+2gamma-2) < 1` for all three cases of `alpha`. This replaces
  1111	the three-case bound on `A_xi(q)` (lines 60-99). The far region and the
  1112	bound on `S(h)` follow lines 101-135, split at the first `M` with
  1113	`h 2^M > 1`, which is `L + 1` of line 121. The corollary follows lines
  1114	155-163. Rows labelled "no direct label (auxiliary to the Lean proof route)"
  1115	serve only this route.
  1116

  1119	not in this module. The rest of `S:wave-variance` (the forms on the full

  2192	
  2193	The main analytic ingredients of the manuscript are not formalized here.
  2194	In particular:
  2195	
  2196	- Existence of the canonical solution and its expansion, including
  2197	  self-pairings and fixed-order coefficients (`P:mild-construction`,
  2198	  `L:joint-fixed-order`), and the crude bound `T:crude`.
  2199	- The upper bound at the scale `t^kappa` (`T:full-upper`) and the Fock-space,
  2200	  Hermite and spectral estimates behind it (`L:fock-form`,
  2201	  `P:static-phase-all-orders`).
  2202	- Equality in law under the exact scaling (`L:exact-canonical-scaling`),
  2203	  beyond the exponent arithmetic listed above.
  2204	- Construction of the operator-valued driver and the Young-type evolution
  2205	  (`P:actual-operator-driver`).
  2206	- Gaussian changes of measure, Cameron-Martin means and tube estimates
  2207	  (`P:raw-block-gaussian-law`, `P:cameron-full-mean`, `P:tube-actual-law`).
  2208	- The variational lower bound and its constant (`T:intrinsic-second-moment`),
  2209	  the occupation ceiling (`T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling`) and the
  2210	  white-noise evaluation (`T:white-moment-bounds`).
  2211	- The moment bounds for the operator paths (`P:radius-actual-moments`,
  2212	  `C:radius-covariance-residuals`), which `RadiusMeanAnchor` takes as a
  2213	  supplied hypothesis.
  2214	- The temporal completion of `L:masked-time-completion` (positive
  2215	  semidefiniteness, the null quotient, separability, the extension from
  2216	  `L^2(0,T)`, the complexification identity, membership of interval
  2217	  amplitudes), which `MaskedTrigProducts` takes as supplied hypotheses
  2218	  (`hmem`, `hmod`) and `MaskedModulation.masked_trig_products_bridged_paper`
  2219	  as `hmem` and `hnorm`. The bound `E:masked-time-schur` and the modulation
  2220	  bound `L:masked-temporal-modulation` are formalized for the defining
  2221	  double integral.
  2222	- The identification of the Rayleigh-form rate with `sqrt(-E_s)` for the
  2223	  spectral bottom of `-Delta - h_s` (`P:variational-unmasked-rate`, needs
  2224	  self-adjoint operators) and of the integral-form cost with `E W(Psi)^2`
  2225	  (`L:compact-raw-profile`, needs Gaussian chaos).
  2226	- The ground family of `S:compact-mean-family` (flows, spectral projections,
  2227	  normalized complement, margins; interface C16), which
  2228	  `IndexedCone` takes as one supplied hypothesis structure.
  2229	- The infinite-dimensional results of `S:compact-gaussian`
  2230	  (`L:cutoff-factorization`, `P:cutoff-singular-values`,
  2231	  `P:compact-two-envelopes`, `L:compact-positive-order`,
  2232	  `P:localized-finite-variance`, `C:finite-gaussian-operators`,
  2233	  `P:cutoff-boundary-tests`): they need Schatten classes, singular values of
  2234	  compact operators and torus Sobolev spaces.
  2235	- `N_0`, the scaling identities and the tails of
  2236	  `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`. (The spectral homogeneity
  2237	  `mu(cA) = c^alpha mu(A)` of its proof is now derived, by characteristic

   150	\chapter{Setting and strategy}\label{S:book-setting}
   151	
   152	\section{Model and standing assumptions}\label{S:model}
   153	
   154	We study the hyperbolic Anderson model
   155	\cite{chen:author2026:time-dependency}*{(1.1)}
   156	\begin{equation}\label{E:HAM}
   157	  \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2}(t,x)=\Delta u(t,x)+\W(t,x)u(t,x),
   158	  \qquad u(0,x)=1,\quad \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}(0,x)=0,
   159	\end{equation}
   160	for $(t,x) \in \R_+\times\R^d$, $d \in \{1,2,3\}$, interpreted in the
   161	Stratonovich sense (limit of classical wave equations driven by smoothed noises
   162	$\W_{\epsilon,\delta}$). The noise is centered Gaussian with
   163	\begin{equation}\label{E:cov}
   164	  \operatorname{Cov}\big(\W(s,x),\W(t,y)\big)=|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}\gamma(x-y),
   165	  \qquad 0<\alpha_0<1,
   166	\end{equation}
   167	where $\gamma \ge 0$ is nonnegative definite with spectral measure $\mu$.
   168	
   169	\begin{hypothesis}[Homogeneous covariance]\label{H:homog}
   170	  Let $d \in \{1,2,3\}$ and $0 < \alpha_0 < 1$. The spatial covariance is a
   171	  nonnegative, even, positive-definite tempered Radon measure $\Gamma$ on
   172	  $\R^d$, with positive even tempered Radon spectral measure $\mu$ in the
   173	  convention
   174	  \[
   175	    \Gamma=\int e^{i\xi\cdot x}\mu(\ud\xi)
   176	    \quad\text{in the sense of tempered distributions}.
   177	  \]
   178	  The symbol $\gamma$ in~\eqref{E:cov} denotes this covariance as a function
   179	  when one exists, and as a distribution otherwise. For every Borel set $A$ and
   180	  $c > 0$, $\Gamma(cA) = c^{d-\alpha}\Gamma(A)$, and
   181	  \begin{equation}\label{E:threshold}
   182	    \alpha_0+\alpha<2,
   183	  \end{equation}
   184	  with $0 < \alpha < d$, or $\alpha = d = 1$. In particular, the last case
   185	  includes spatial white noise $\Gamma = \delta_0$.
   186	\end{hypothesis}
   187	
   188	Throughout we write
   189	\begin{equation}\label{E:kappa}
   190	  \kappa:=\frac{4-\alpha-\alpha_0}{3-\alpha}\in(1,2).
   191	\end{equation}
   192	
   193	\paragraph{Contribution of the present work.}
   194	We address the second moment of the original Stratonovich solution with
   195	fractional temporal covariance throughout Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}. The
   196	independent upper bound reaches the scale $t^\kappa$, rather than only the
   197	coarse quadratic exponential scale in the source. The main identification gives
   198	an intrinsic variational expression for the limiting constant over all
   199	nonnegative smooth compact spacetime controls, without a separability
   200	restriction. It retains the covariance amplitude, kinetic coefficient one and a
   201	Gaussian cost equal to one half of the variance, and includes the zero
   202	covariance case. The upper and lower comparisons refer to the same canonical
   203	solution. The occupation and spatial-energy estimates then give bounds on this
   204	constant; evaluating the white spatial energy is not a numerical evaluation of
   205	the full moment supremum. The earlier results discussed below concern different
   206	stochastic interpretations or temporal covariances and do not supply this
   207	identification by substitution.
   208	
   209	Figure~\ref{Fig:proof-map} summarizes the main dependencies.
   210	\input{notes/figures/proof-map}
   211	
   212	\paragraph{Main result and dependencies.}
   213	Theorem~\ref{T:intrinsic-second-moment} identifies the original point-moment
   214	limit for every covariance in Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}. Its full variational
   215	domain and normalization are displayed in~\eqref{E:intrinsic-positive-formula}.
   216	Theorem~\ref{T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling} and
   217	Corollary~\ref{C:intrinsic-spatial-bracket} give derived bounds;
   218	Section~\ref{S:intrinsic-white-evaluation} evaluates the white spatial energy
   219	and its resulting moment bounds. These bounds need not be attained at the moment
   220	constant.
   221	
   222	The independent earlier Theorem~\ref{T:full-upper} establishes finite upper
   223	growth at scale $t^\kappa$ and precedes its uses proving variational finiteness.
   224	It uses the fixed-order construction proved in Lemma~\ref{L:joint-fixed-order},
   225	the Gaussian and complex phase estimates in
     1	\section{Covariance bounds for physically masked wave fields}
     2	\label{S:masked-covariance}
     3	
     4	We establish the covariance estimates needed for the operator construction.
     5	Throughout this section, Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} holds, $a = \alpha_0$, and
     6	$\Gamma \ne 0$. For zero spatial covariance, the spatial spectral measures and
     7	noise variances vanish; the purely temporal estimates remain valid independently
     8	of $\Gamma$. We use the unitary Fourier transform
     9	\[
    10	  \widehat{f}(\xi) = c_d\int_{\R^d}e^{-i\xi\cdot x}f(x)\ud x,
    11	  \qquad c_d = (2\pi)^{-d/2}.
    12	\]
    13	The spectral convention in Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} means that, for every
    14	complex Schwartz test $\varphi$,
    15	\begin{equation}\label{E:masked-spectral-convention}
    16	  \int_{\R^d}\varphi(x)\Gamma(\ud x)
    17	  = \int_{\R^d}\left(\int_{\R^d}e^{i\xi\cdot x}
    18	  \varphi(x)\ud x\right)\mu(\ud\xi).
    19	\end{equation}
    20	This is an identity of distribution pairings. We will not interchange two
    21	infinite measures in the associated oscillatory expression.
    22	
    23	A positive tempered Radon measure has polynomial mass growth. Indeed, choose a
    24	nonnegative compact smooth test that is at least one on the unit ball, and apply
    25	a defining Schwartz seminorm bound for the distribution to its dilations. Its
    26	mass on a ball of radius $R \ge 1$ is bounded by a power of $R$. Summation over
    27	dyadic shells then gives integrability of $(1+|x|)^{-N}$ for some $N$, and hence
    28	absolute integrability of every Schwartz test. These facts apply to both
    29	$\Gamma$ and $\mu$. Smooth cutoffs converge in the Schwartz topology, so these
    30	integrals agree with the tempered pairings.
    31	
    32	\subsection{Translated spectral growth and physical masks}
    33	
    34	\begin{proposition}[Translated spectral mass]\label{P:masked-spectral-growth}
    35	  Put
    36	  \[
    37	    M_\Gamma = \int_{\R^d}e^{-|x|^2/4}\Gamma(\ud x),
    38	    \qquad C_\Gamma = \frac{eM_\Gamma}{(2\sqrt{\pi})^d}.
    39	  \]
    40	  Then $0 < M_\Gamma < \infty$, and for $y \in \R^d$ and $r > 0$,
    41	  \begin{align}
    42	    \int_{\R^d}e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}\mu(\ud\xi)
    43	    &= \left(\frac{r}{2\sqrt{\pi}}\right)^d
    44	    \int_{\R^d}e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}e^{-iy\cdot x}\Gamma(\ud x),
    45	    \label{E:masked-gaussian-transform}\\
    46	    0 \le \int_{\R^d}e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}\mu(\ud\xi)
    47	    &\le \frac{r^\alpha M_\Gamma}{(2\sqrt{\pi})^d},
    48	    \qquad \mu(B(y,r)) \le C_\Gamma r^\alpha.
    49	    \label{E:masked-translated-ball}
    50	  \end{align}
    51	  The ball may be open or closed.
    52	\end{proposition}
    53	
    54	\begin{proof}
    55	  Temperedness gives finiteness of $M_\Gamma$. Its positivity follows from
    56	  $\Gamma \ne 0$. To check the Fourier constant, set $J(b) = \int_\R
    57	  e^{-Ax^2}e^{ibx}\ud x$ for $A > 0$. Squaring the real Gaussian integral and
    58	  using polar coordinates gives $J(0) = \sqrt{\pi/A}$. Differentiation and
    59	  integration by parts give $J'(b) = -bJ(b)/(2A)$. Therefore, $J(b) =
    60	  \sqrt{\pi/A}e^{-b^2/(4A)}$. Taking products over the coordinates gives
    61	  \[
    62	    \int_{\R^d}e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}e^{i(\xi-y)\cdot x}\ud x
    63	    = \left(\frac{2\sqrt{\pi}}r\right)^d e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}.
    64	  \]
    65	  Apply~\eqref{E:masked-spectral-convention} to the single Schwartz test
    66	  $e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}e^{-iy\cdot x}$ to obtain \eqref{E:masked-gaussian-transform}.
    67	  Its left side is nonnegative. Taking the absolute value on the right removes
    68	  the complex phase because $\Gamma$ is nonnegative. The pushforward of $\Gamma$
    69	  by $x \mapsto rx$ assigns mass $r^{\alpha-d}\Gamma(A)$ to a Borel set $A$.
    70	  Thus,
    71	  \[
    72	    \int e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}\Gamma(\ud x) = r^{\alpha-d}M_\Gamma.
    73	  \]
    74	  This proves the Gaussian bound. On either ball $B(y,r)$ the integrand
    75	  $e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}$ is at least $e^{-1}$, proving the mass bound. This proves
    76	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-spectral-growth}.
    77	\end{proof}
    78	
    79	Choose and fix a real nonzero Schwartz function $\zeta$. For $R > 0$ put
    80	$\zeta_R(x) = \zeta(x/R)$, $k_R = \widehat{\zeta_R}$ and $L =
    81	\|\widehat{\zeta}\|_1$. Then $k_R(u) = R^d\widehat{\zeta}(Ru)$ and $\|k_R\|_1 =
    82	L > 0$. Define
    83	\begin{equation}\label{E:masked-auxiliary-measure}
    84	  \nu_R(\ud\eta) = \rho_R(\eta)\ud\eta,
    85	  \qquad \rho_R(\eta) = c_d^2L\int |k_R(\xi-\eta)|\mu(\ud\xi).
   285	  by parts gives the masked marginal $-I_\chi\chi(x_1)^2$. Thus, $V(g) = 0$ and
   286	  $V(\zeta g) = J_\chi I_\chi^2 > 0$. For a nonzero nonnegative $\tau \in
   287	  C_c^\infty(0,T)$, set $F(t,x) = \tau(t)g(x)$. The temporal factor
   288	  $\|\tau\|_a^2$ is finite and strictly positive because its nonnegative
   289	  integrand is positive on a set of positive two-dimensional measure.
   290	  Consequently, the full unmasked variance is zero and the masked variance is
   291	  positive. This proves Proposition~\ref{P:masked-quotient-obstruction}.
   292	\end{proof}

   294	\subsection{Temporal modulation and continuous wave factors}
   295	
   296	Write $\langle x\rangle = \sqrt{1+x^2}$. Let $I = [s,s+h] \subset [0,T]$, with
   297	$0 < h \le 1$. Norms below are those of the complexified temporal completion in
   298	Lemma~\ref{L:masked-time-completion}.
   299	
   300	\begin{lemma}[Modulated amplitudes]\label{L:masked-temporal-modulation}
   301	  Let $A \in C^1(I;\mathbb{C})$, $M = \sup_I|A|$ and $D = \sup_I|A'|$. For every
   302	  real $\omega$,
   303	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-temporal-modulation}
   304	    \|1_IA(t)e^{i\omega t}\|_a^2
   305	    \le C_0(a)h^{2-a}(M+hD)^2\langle h\omega\rangle^{a-1},
   306	    \qquad C_0(a) = \frac{16}{1-a}.
   307	  \end{equation}
   308	  The bound is uniform in $T,s,h,A$ and $\omega$.
   309	\end{lemma}
   310	
   311	\begin{proof}
   312	  Put $c(v) = \int_s^{s+h-v}A(u+v)\overline{A(u)}\ud u$ for $0 \le v \le h$.
   313	  Differentiation at the moving endpoint gives
   314	  \[
   315	    c'(v) = -A(s+h)\overline{A(s+h-v)}
   316	    +\int_s^{s+h-v}A'(u+v)\overline{A(u)}\ud u.
   317	  \]
   318	  Thus, $c(h) = 0$, $|c(v)| \le hM^2$ and $|c'(v)| \le M^2+hMD$. Splitting the
   319	  covariance square into its two conjugate triangles gives
   320	  \[
   321	    \|1_IA(t)e^{i\omega t}\|_a^2
   322	    = 2\operatorname{Re}\int_0^h v^{-a}e^{i\omega v}c(v)\ud v
   323	    = 2h^{2-a}\operatorname{Re}\int_0^1 y^{-a}e^{i\omega hy}f(y)\ud y,
   324	  \]
   325	  where $f(y) = c(hy)/h$. Set $K = M+hD$. Then $f(1) = 0$ and $|f|,|f'| \le
   326	  K^2$. If $K = 0$ the assertion is immediate. If $|\omega h| \le 1$, the last
   327	  integral is at most $K^2/(1-a)$ in absolute value, and $\langle\omega
   328	  h\rangle^{a-1} \ge 2^{(a-1)/2}$. The claimed constant is sufficient in this
   329	  case.
   330	
   331	  Now suppose $k = |\omega h| > 1$. On $[0,1/k]$ the integral is at most
   332	  $K^2k^{a-1}/(1-a)$. On $[1/k,1]$, integrate the exponential by parts. The
   333	  endpoint at one vanishes, while the other endpoint contributes at most
   334	  $K^2k^{a-1}$. The derivative integral, divided by $k$, is bounded by
   335	  \[
   336	    \frac{K^2}k\left(a\int_{1/k}^1 y^{-a-1}\ud y
   337	    +\int_{1/k}^1 y^{-a}\ud y\right)
   338	    \le K^2 k^{a-1}\left(1+\frac1{1-a}\right).
   339	  \]
   340	  Here $k^{-1} \le k^{a-1}$ since $a > 0$. The total is at most
   341	  $4K^2k^{a-1}/(1-a)$. Finally, $k^{a-1} \le \sqrt{2}\langle\omega
   342	  h\rangle^{a-1}$ and $8\sqrt{2} \le 16$. Including the factor $2h^{2-a}$ proves
   343	  the bound for either sign of $\omega$. This proves
   344	  Lemma~\ref{L:masked-temporal-modulation}.
   345	\end{proof}

   375	  used. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:masked-trig-products}.
